text.p: Turkish t-bill and bond yields closed sharply lower on Friday after a cabinet decree was published in the official gazette late on Thursday to impose a 10 percent witholding tax on interest income from government securities to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1.
Although t-bill and bond yields fell, overnight money rates kept 74.75-75 percent levels all day and the central bank lent banks 3.7 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent to meet weekend cash demand.

Bankers said cash shortage eased as the market opened only 4.8 trillion lira short after 57 trillion lira on Thursday when the central bank injected 34.5 trillion lira via overnight funding and 7-day repos.

Bankers said yields in the bond market dived by around four percentage points in early morning trade because the decree buoyed demand for outstanding papers, but slightly recovered on profit-taking afterwards.
The tax will not apply to outstanding t-bills and bonds having 1997 maturities, according to the cabinet decree.
The average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 bond closed at 115.04 percent versus Thursday's 117.88 after sinking to a low of 113.25 earlier in the day.
The average overnight repo rate also dropped to 73.83 percent from yesterday's 76.72 percent.
Yields in the bond market had been rising due to cash shortage since the markets reopened on Wednesday following a 1-1/2 day official holiday.
The government expects a 170 trillion lira income from the witholding tax in 1997, as part of its second revenue-raising package unveiled on September 19.
Turkish lira closed weaker at 96,430 to the dollar after seeing a low of 96,510 against Thursday's 96,150 close, in line with the movements in the dollar/mark parity.
